stories.title: Thrive Capital led VCs into pro sports ownership; Collaborative Fund just upped that play
stories.summary:
Collaborative Fund, a fifteen year old New York based venture firm with roughly one billion dollars under management, is taking a stake in D.C. United and Audi Field. The deal needs approval from Major League Soccer.

This makes Collaborative the latest firm to follow a path opened by Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital. Thrive Capital turned venture money into sports ownership by launching Thrive Eternal to hold franchises for decades. Thrive previously bought the San Francisco Giants and the Lakers for twelve point five billion dollars. Thrive built a permanent capital vehicle to hold trophy assets. Collaborative is investing directly out of its early stage fund, treating the deal like infrastructure.

Collaborative founder Craig Shapiro framed the investment as an extension of the firm's work. He wrote that a franchise is the ultimate consumer product. Shapiro pointed to tailwinds in American soccer, including upcoming major events and rising youth participation. He also highlighted D.C. United owning Audi Field in Washington, D.C., a talent development pipeline through Loudoun County, Virginia, and rights to a future Baltimore expansion team.

Collaborative plans to use Audi Field as a showcase for its portfolio companies. This includes integrating Whoop wearables and Olipop game day drinks. The investment also benefits from soaring team valuations. D.C. United’s valuation climbed from thirty-five million dollars in two thousand eight to seven hundred eighty-five million dollars today. This valuation includes Audi Field and surrounding real estate.
stories.author: Connie Loizos

stories.title: Under-construction bridge collapses in Bihar’s Vaishali, seven injured
stories.summary:
Seven people were injured on Thursday, September tenth, twenty twenty-six. Part of an under-construction four-lane bridge collapsed in Bihar's Vaishali district.

The bridge is part of a major road transport scheme. It is backed by the Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

The incident happened near Itwaripur village in the Lalganj police station area. A technical issue happened in the girder system during movement on the Bakarpur-Manikpur section of N. H. one thirty-nine W.

One worker remained trapped under heavy machinery for about an hour and a half. He sustained a leg fracture before rescuers saved him with a gas cutter.

All seven injured workers received first aid treatment. Three of them were sent to Sadar Hospital in Hajipur for better care.

The National Highway Authority of India is doing a detailed technical assessment. They want to find out what caused the malfunction.

Meanwhile, Leader of Opposition, Tejashwi Yadav blamed corruption for the accident. He said substandard construction materials cause continuous bridge collapses in the state.

stories.title: Lawsuit challenges intimidation of DHS observers across the country
stories.summary:
A new federal lawsuit challenges what it calls a nationwide policy of intimidation and retaliation. The complaint was filed on Thursday in Washington, D. C.

Minneapolis resident Michael Khalili and the nonprofit Common Cause brought the action. They filed the ninety-four-page complaint against the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Justice, the F. B. I., and other agencies.

The lawsuit accuses the federal government of violating the First Amendment and privacy rights. This affects observers in Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, Illinois, Maine, and Tennessee.

The legal action asks a judge for national relief. It wants to bar federal agencies from intimidating or retaliating against legal observers.

The complaint outlines encounters faced by seven Common Cause members and other activists. They were photographed, followed, pepper-sprayed, and threatened with police visits. They were also subjected to facial recognition databases, administrative subpoenas, and the revocation of trusted traveler statuses like Global Entry.

The complaint highlights the case of Michael Khalili. He is a forty-seven-year-old father of two. He stopped observing Immigration and Customs Enforcement following pressure from his family and tense exchanges with federal officers.

Law enforcement queried his state motor vehicle records fifty-five times since March of twenty twenty-six. That compares to just twice before he began observing. His Global Entry status was revoked one day after an encounter with immigration officers. It was later reinstated following a journalist's inquiry.

The lawsuit argues these actions stem from top-down Trump administration directives. These include National Security Presidential Memorandum seven and associated Department of Justice memos. The directives link impeding immigration enforcement to domestic terrorism. They also repeal guardrails on facial recognition and license plate readers.

Danielle Lang is the vice president of voting rights and rule of law at the Campaign Legal Center. Her organization is litigating the case. She stated that the events described are a top-down policy of retaliation that needs to be addressed.

Maryam Jazini Dorcheh is the Common Cause vice president for litigation. She said the right of citizens to criticize and hold the government accountable is under attack. She added that criminalizing peaceful observation hinders their mission.

The Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Justice did not provide an immediate response to the allegations. The F. B. I. declined to comment.
stories.author: Jude Joffe-Block

stories.title: Anthropic caught scientists using Claude to further biological weapon research
stories.summary: Anthropic caught scientists using Claude to further biological weapon research. The company shared this new report on Thursday. The findings include five case studies of models being used to develop biological weapons. They also include safety measures and company responses. In one instance from May, Anthropic caught a flagged request. The request asked Claude to author a grant for gain-of-function research. The research focused on the chikungunya virus. That is a pathogen with no licensed treatment that causes debilitating symptoms. The proposal sought to genetically alter the virus. It aimed to increase its transmissibility and immune response evasion. The proposal originated from a military research institute. The company took similar issue with gain-of-function research into bird flu. A separate case involved a researcher using Claude for different work. The researcher built an atlas of venom toxin peptides. They also built a generative pipeline that optimized toxin characteristics. The full report includes case studies on other topics. Those topics are models being used as a surveillance tool, software exploits, propaganda, and weapons systems. Jacob Klein is Anthropic's head of threat intelligence. He told The New York Times that the situations are incredibly nuanced. He stated you do not see someone in a comic book kind of way wanting to build a biological weapon to kill everybody. Detecting misuse is complicated. Research into a new vaccine could look a lot like creating a bioweapon. This prompted Anthropic to err on the side of caution due to potential consequences. The company banned the accounts of anyone misusing Claude or Anthropic models. Anthropic is using the findings to further improve safeguards. The company is not naming the individuals or institutions involved. Anthropic noted that the implicated parties are working scientists. The company does not assert that they intended harm. Identifying them could expose them to harm.
stories.author: staff@engadget.com (Ian Carlos Campbell)

stories.title: New genomic tool for clams boosts sustainable aquaculture
stories.summary:
Researchers have developed the first high density genotyping platform for two economically vital clam species. These are the Japanese clam and the common clam. The team includes researchers from C. I. I. M. A. R. Their study was published in the journal Aquaculture. The study introduces a new S. N. P. chip with approximately sixty-three thousand genetic markers.

This tool helps produce clams that are more resistant to disease and climate change. It also helps conserve genetic diversity. More than forty-five thousand markers have been validated for the Japanese clam. Another fifteen thousand markers are validated for the common clam. The platform enables the identification of kinship and the monitoring of genetic diversity. It also tracks inbreeding levels.

The Aquatic Animal Health group identified more than thirteen thousand markers related to resistance against a specific parasite. That parasite is known as Perkinsus olsenii. According to the researchers, this tool will support coastal communities in the future. It allows new genetic improvement programs for both species of clam. This will have a significant impact on the blue economy sector.

The project involved several partner institutions. They include the University of Padua and the University of Santiago de Compostela. Other partners are the Roslin Institute at the University of Edinburgh and the Institut Universitaire Européen de la Mer. Aquaculture genetics companies Benchmark Genetics and Thermo Fisher Scientific also joined the project. The openly available platform aims to accelerate selective breeding. It also supports marine conservation amid ongoing production declines. These declines are caused by habitat degradation, climate change, and disease.

stories.title: OpenAI puts Pro subscriptions on hold due to Astra demand
stories.summary:
OpenAI has temporarily paused new sign-ups for its two hundred dollars per month Pro subscription tier. This is due to unprecedented infrastructure strain driven by demand for its newest and most powerful model named Astra.

Sottiaux stated that the move was intended as the smallest step to maintain the broadest access possible. He wrote that they wanted to continue giving access while managing the load.

OpenAI has other service tiers that remain available to users. These include the A. P. I. and the lower cost Go and Plus plans.

The company warned on Wednesday that restrictions might be necessary. Sottiaux previously described the demand for Astra as unprecedented and unlike anything seen during the company past periods of steep growth.

Astra was launched on September third. It has been rolling out across Pro, Plus, Enterprise, and Business accounts.

OpenAI heralded the model as a generational leap and the beginning of the artificial general intelligence era. The company has not disclosed how long the Pro subscriptions will remain disabled. They also have not released daily sign up figures to quantify the scale of the demand.
stories.author: Sarah Perez

stories.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
stories.summary:
LinkedIn has won the dismissal of two class-action lawsuits over scanning browser extensions. Judge Vince Chhabria granted the motion to dismiss on Tuesday. The judge said the plaintiffs failed to establish legal standing. Neither user proved they had browser extensions installed that sent private data to LinkedIn.

The judge gave the plaintiffs a chance to amend their complaints. He expressed deep skepticism about their future chances. He wrote that users voluntarily download browser extensions. These tools intentionally expose data to websites by their very nature. It seems unlikely the plaintiffs will ever prove a privacy violation.

The lawsuits were filed separately in April. Attorney J. R. Howell represents one of the plaintiffs. He is evaluating whether to refile the claims in a California state court. That court operates under different standing requirements. He is also considering an appeal in the U. S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.
stories.author: Jon Brodkin

stories.title: Man Utd cruise past Sabah on Champions League return with 4-0 win
stories.summary:
Manchester United returned to the C. H. Champions League after a three-season absence. They secured a four-nil win against competition debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan at Old Trafford on Thursday.

Following a slow start that drew minor groans from the home crowd, United stormed into a three-goal lead by half-time. Matheus Cunha opened the scoring in the twenty-seventh minute. He tapped in a low cross from Patrick Dorgu, following a nervy moment that included an early missed header by Sabah player, Joy-Lance Mickels.

Benjamin Sesko added the third just before the break. He rounded the goalkeeper and slotted home from a tight angle.

Lisandro Martinez rounded off the victory in the second half. He tapped in from a goal-line scramble after a corner.

United manager Michael Carrick used all five substitutions with more than twenty minutes remaining. This allowed the team to rest players ahead of this Sunday's Manchester derby.

The victory is described as one of the biggest mismatches in C. H. Champions League history. It does not erase underlying concerns from United's start to the domestic season. That run has yielded only four points from their first three Premier League games.

stories.title: BRICS 2026: Delhi braces for traffic diversions from 2 pm to 8:30 pm tomorrow, check alternate routes, diversion points
stories.summary: Delhi commuters face extensive travel disruptions on Friday, September eleventh. Traffic regulations and diversions take effect for the B. R. I. C. S. Summit. The summit happens at Bharat Mandapam in Pragati Maidan. The restrictions operate from two p m to eight thirty p m. They impact more than thirty-five roads and twenty-two designated diversion points. These affect central and south Delhi, the airport corridors, and railway stations. The high profile summit runs from September eleventh to September thirteenth. It brings foreign delegations and very important person motorcades to the national capital. Nearly forty-eight hundred traffic personnel are deployed by Delhi Police to manage security arrangements. Non-destined commercial vehicles are barred from entering Delhi. Emergency and medical vehicles retain priority passage. Roadside parking within two hundred metres of controlled corridors is prohibited. The traffic plan lists numerous regulated routes. These include Sardar Patel Marg, Shanti Path, Akbar Road, Mathura Road, and Ashoka Road. There are twenty-two diversion points. Locations include areas around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Dhaula Kuan, Moti Bagh, and Lodhi Road. Traffic may be stopped at short notice during very important person movements. This creates uncertainty and congestion on connecting corridors. The Delhi Traffic Police strongly recommends using the Metro. This is particularly true for airport-bound passengers. Alternative routes are established for travellers heading to Indira Gandhi International Airport from Gurugram, Dwarka, and various parts of the city. Other routes help those commuting to New Delhi, Old Delhi, and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.

stories.title: Is AI Actually Going to Kill Us All?
stories.summary: This week on the W. I. R. E. D. podcast Uncanny Valley, artificial intelligence researcher, Jacob Coxon, resigned from Anthropic. His resignation went viral after he published a thread on X warning that leading labs are behaving irresponsibly. Coxon claimed that the people building these systems earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This timeline was reinforced by an Anthropic senior safety executive who publicly agreed with the sentiment. W. I. R. E. D. senior correspondent, Will Knight, noted that Anthropic has historically built its safety pitch around existential risk. However, this public departure signals growing alarm over rapid developments. These developments include OpenAI solving a Clay mathematics puzzle within days. Labs are also accelerating recursive self-improvement where artificial intelligence is used to enhance its own code. Knight expressed skepticism regarding existential doom percentages. He pointed out that recent agent misbehavior often stems from systems being unintelligent rather than hyper-competent. Despite that, he remains concerned about corporate concentration of power and vulnerabilities arising from rushed cyber-capable model releases. Additionally, the U. S. Census Bureau published a misleading report claiming noncitizens voted in the twenty twenty election. W. I. R. E. D. uncovered evidence showing the Census Bureau report used very faulty data to reach its conclusions. Finally, Apple debuted its first folding phone called the iPhone Duo with a price tag of roughly two thousand dollars.
stories.author: Brian Barrett, Leah Feiger, Will Knight

stories.title: NASA Answers President’s Call to Establish United States Space Academy
stories.summary:
National Aeronautics and Space Administration Administrator Jared Isaacman chaired the first Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy meeting on September ninth. The meeting followed an Executive Order signed by President Donald Trump to create the institution.

Isaacman and Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson met with key officials at National Aeronautics and Space Administration Headquarters in Washington. Those officials included United States Chief Technology Officer Ethan Klein. They discussed governance, curriculum, service commitments, and partnerships for the academy.

Responses to the Request for Information will help inform the path forward for the commission. Those responses are due by six p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on Monday, October twenty-sixth. Each state is allowed one submission through its governor designee.

The commission operates under a one hundred twenty day mandate. It must develop recommendations for President Trump to build the technical talent and leadership pipeline for America in space.

The timeline outlines groundbreaking no later than twenty twenty-seven. The academy will temporarily host the first three hundred students in twenty twenty-eight. A permanent location will be in operation by twenty thirty-one.

Isaacman shared his thoughts after the meeting. He stated that the first commission meeting made clear how much talent and commitment stand behind the vision of President Trump for the United States Space Academy.
stories.author: Lauren E. Low

stories.title: Digital data leeches: trading on our profiles
stories.summary:
About twelve thousand app users in Britain sued the dating app Grindr. They claimed the app shared sensitive personal information like H. I. V. status with advertisers. The lawsuit was filed in twenty twenty-four and was settled earlier this week. Grindr agreed to pay claimants a total of twenty-six million pounds. That equals approximately thirty million euros or thirty-five million dollars. The company stressed that the settlement is not an admission of liability. They continue to dispute the allegations and noted there has been no legal judgement.

The case highlights broader concerns about data privacy. People worry about how information entrusted to apps is handled by cloud services and advertising networks., Jan Penfrat, a digital policy expert for European Digital Rights, spoke about the issue. He stated that many big tech companies want to make tracking difficult for users and regulators. They try to hide what data is gathered on devices and for what purpose.

The European Union enforces strict rules like the General Data Protection Regulation. They also use the Digital Markets Act and the Digital Services Act. In twenty twenty-five, the E. U. Commission handed out massive fines. They fined Apple five hundred million euros, Meta two hundred million euros, and Google eight hundred ninety million euros., Jan Penfrat noted that these sums are tiny amounts. Companies like Google or Amazon make that much money in just a few days. This allows them to simply include fines in their regular budgets. Effective oversight is further complicated by other factors. Europe relies heavily on cloud services and operating systems provided by American companies. There is also a lack of political will in Brussels. Officials fail to properly equip European data protection authorities and take firmer action.

stories.title: Natural feedbacks will warm world an extra 20 per cent this century
stories.summary: Natural carbon emissions from ecosystems will amplify global warming by twenty to thirty percent this century. This is according to a new study led by, Christina Schädel at the Woodwell Climate Research Center in Massachusetts. Climate models include several global feedback loops. Yet no single model accounts for all ecosystem feedbacks. Now, a study has shown that these natural feedbacks will heat the planet by an extra zero point two degrees Celsius to zero point four degrees Celsius by twenty one hundred. This warming comes on top of at least one degree Celsius to two degree Celsius of global warming already expected between now and then. Even in a scenario in which emissions start declining today, the feedbacks add zero point two degrees Celsius of extra warming this century. This prolongs global warming because there is a lag between when emissions occur and when the temperature impacts occur. In a climate scenario in which human emissions decline after twenty fifty, the natural feedbacks add an average of zero point four degrees Celsius of warming by twenty one hundred. The study examines four major natural feedbacks. The first involves thawing Arctic permafrost, where microbes decompose ancient organic matter and release carbon dioxide and methane. The second involves wetlands, where warmer water and increased microbial activity release more methane. The third involves ponds and lakes experiencing those same methane-releasing processes. The fourth feedback is driven by hotter air, shorter winters, and drier soils that increase the frequency and intensity of wildfires. This results in greater carbon dioxide and methane emissions. These emissions are currently left out of carbon budgets. Tim Lenton at the University of Exeter notes the findings. He says the findings suggest we are going to go further over one point five degrees Celsius global warming than we thought. This brings all the extra risks. It requires governments to invest even more in measures like flood barriers, drought-resistant crops, and early-warning systems for climate tipping points. It also requires governments to fully account for all sources of emissions that contribute to warming when planning for the future.
stories.author: Alec Luhn

stories.title: Trump's $1 trillion-plus 'dividend' plan meets immediate bipartisan pushback
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump announced a proposal to give every adult American citizen a five thousand dollar dividend. This is conditional on a Republican victory in November during an affordability-focused midterm election.

Two hundred forty-five point three million US adult citizens exist according to twenty twenty-four Census data. Giving them five thousand dollars apiece would cost north of one point two trillion dollars.

The proposal immediately drew bipartisan criticism from some of Trump's own supporters. It raised questions regarding whether it could violate federal laws prohibiting payments intended to influence votes.

Palantir co-founder and Republican donor, Joe Lonsdale, criticized the plan on the platform X as bread and circus bribes. Representative Chip Roy, a Republican from Texas and a leader of the Freedom Caucus, told Politico that he would like to know how they plan to pay for it. Former House Freedom Caucus Chair, Bob Good, said on X that it is a socialist vote-buying scheme.

Trump and Vice President, J. D. Vance, asserted that the payments would be funded by revenues generated from administration tariffs. The Penn Wharton Budget Model estimates those import duties have brought in around three hundred billion dollars in total between January twenty-five and July twenty-six. More than one hundred billion dollars of that was refunded since February when the Supreme Court struck down a swath of tariffs as illegal.

National debt recently passed the forty trillion dollar mark. The US national deficit is nearing one point eight trillion dollars for the fiscal year to date. The government has spent more than six trillion dollars between October and July.

Trump was asked in a Fox News interview why the payments are withheld until after the midterms. He said because the Democrats can't do it.

stories.title: Secret son revelation ignites bitter succession dispute in Ugandan kingdom
stories.summary:
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi the fourth died on August twenty-seventh in the United States. King Oyo ascended the throne in nineteen ninety-five at the age of three as the world's youngest reigning monarch. He was unmarried and not publicly known to have children.

The royal clan succession committee chose Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma as crown prince on Wednesday. He works as a news anchor and editor at the public broadcaster U. B. C.

However, hours later, Oyo's sister Princess Ruth Nsemere Komuntale and Queen Mother Best Kemigisa Akiiki rejected the selection. They cited a will left by the late king directing that an unpublicized biological son succeed him. Tooro prime minister Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki first revealed the existence of the heir on August twenty-seventh.

The Queen Mother denounced the committee's choice. She stated that the royal family had been placed under house arrest after troops removed royal guards and surrounded the palace.

Another contender, London amateur football goalkeeper Prince George Desmond-Kamurasi, declined the throne due to other responsibilities. Andrew Mwenda and a committee member noted traditional requirements regarding a successor. A king's son must be born to an officially married queen and introduced to elders.

King Oyo is scheduled to be buried on Saturday at the Karambi royal tombs in Fort Portal, western Uganda. Tooro is one of five ancient kingdoms recognized by the Ugandan government. Monarchs wield vast social influence there but hold no political authority.
stories.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies

stories.title: Can Trump really pay $5,000 to every American adult?
stories.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced an offer of five thousand dollars to every adult American if Republicans win November's midterm elections. The proposal would cost the United States government approximately one point three trillion dollars for the nation's nearly two hundred seventy million adults. Democrats labelled it an empty promise. Speaking at a party convention in Texas on Wednesday, Trump stated the funds would have to be spent domestically. He provided no details on how the payments would be funded or monitored and did not specify whether he would seek legislative approval from Congress. Vice-President J. D. Vance suggested on Fox News that the payouts could be funded by tariff revenue and restricted from wealthy Americans. However, historical data from the Bipartisan Policy Center shows the United States has brought in roughly four hundred seventy-five billion dollars in tariff and excise tax revenue since the beginning of twenty twenty-five. More than one hundred billion dollars of that total was subsequently refunded following a Supreme Court ruling. The announcement has raised legal and financial questions. Under federal law, payments intended to influence voting are illegal, but legal experts are divided and state it is unlikely the president could approve such a sum via a presidential executive order. Doctor Joan Mahoney at the University of Southampton told the B. B. C. she believes the offer is legal because it would go to everyone regardless of how they voted, though she noted it sounds a bit like a bribe. Meanwhile, Laurel Rapp, director of the United States and North America programme at Chatham House, told the B. B. C. that Trump's offer seemed to be a very different and very transactional agreement made because poor polling threatens Republican control of Congress. Erica York, a senior economist at the Tax Foundation, noted she would be extremely surprised if Congress approved the proposal amid growing national deficits.
key_points: President Donald Trump offered five thousand dollars to every adult American if Republicans win November's midterm elections.
The proposal would cost approximately one point three trillion dollars for nearly two hundred seventy million adults.
Democrats labelled the offer an empty promise, and White House spokesman Davis Ingle defended the administration.
Vice-President J. D. Vance suggested tariff revenue could fund the plan, though historical collection totals are lower.
Legal experts are divided on whether the conditional cash offer violates federal laws against vote-buying.
Erica York of the Tax Foundation stated she would be extremely surprised if Congress approved the plan amid growing deficits.

stories.title: England's push for two-day win halted by weather
stories.summary: England missed a rare two-day Test victory against Pakistan at Edgbaston when bad weather halted their charge at seventeen oh seven B. S. T. on day two. Pakistan closed on fifty-two for two, trailing by two hundred sixty-eight runs to avoid an innings defeat. Ollie Robinson dismissed Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique for ducks in the opening over of the second innings. Play could have continued until nineteen hundred B. S. T., but persistent rain forced an early close. The players return on Friday to complete a three to zero series clean sweep. England began Thursday on one hundred fifty-six for four with a twenty-three run lead. They posted four hundred fifty-three, building a massive first-innings advantage of three hundred twenty runs. The total featured seventy-five from Harry Brook, sixty-nine by Jamie Smith, sixty-five scored by Dan Lawrence, sixty by Emilio Gay, and fifty from Robinson. Razaullah claimed four for one hundred forty-eight for Pakistan, while Josh Tongue took four for forty-two as Pakistan were previously dismissed for one hundred thirty with Shakeel scoring forty-three. Despite dominance, none of England's batters registered a century in the series, leaving Ben Duckett's ton against New Zealand at Trent Bridge as the home side's only hundred of the summer. Under the captaincy of Root, contrasting with the prior regime under Ben Stokes and coach Brendon McCullum where England lost the final Test in each of their past six series, the team showcased a ruthless edge. Brook and Lawrence shared an eighty-six run stand before Brook was run out. Lawrence later chopped on off Mohammad Imran for sixty-five, while Smith kept wicket until suffering a bruised finger that brought in Jordan Cox. Jofra Archer added thirty-two not out with two sixes before Tongue was caught behind.
key_points: England reached four hundred fifty-three in their first innings to lead Pakistan by three hundred twenty runs.
Bad weather stopped play at seventeen oh seven B. S. T. with Pakistan on fifty-two for two.
Ollie Robinson dismissed Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique for ducks in the first over of Pakistan's second innings.
Harry Brook scored seventy-five, Jamie Smith sixty-nine, Dan Lawrence sixty-five, Emilio Gay sixty, and Robinson fifty for England.
Ben Duckett's ton against New Zealand remains the home side's only hundred of the summer.
Root's England approach the final match aiming for a three to zero series clean sweep on Friday.

stories.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
stories.summary: Bioengineer, César de la Fuente and his team search the genomes of living and extinct organisms for new antimicrobials. Drug resistant microbes are a growing global threat. Bacterial antimicrobial resistance was associated with about five million deaths in twenty twenty-one. That annual toll is projected to roughly double by twenty fifty., César de la Fuente stated that antimicrobial resistance is one of the greatest existential threats to humanity. He noted that the world has not had a new class of antibiotics for fifty years. His lab uses deep learning models alongside C. H. A. T. G. P. T. and Codex to brainstorm hypotheses. These tools help write and refine code, process datasets, analyze results, and bridge gaps between team members from biology, chemistry, computer science, and engineering. Traditional methods of discovering new antimicrobial candidates can take years. Artificial intelligence tools help reduce that initial search phase down from years to hours. The tools work by scanning vast genome and protein databases to identify functional patterns., César de la Fuente uses C. H. A. T. G. P. T. as a collaborative sounding board and brainstorming partner. He cautions that researchers must always double check artificial intelligence output for accuracy.

stories.title: 3 ways to prep for your next big race with Search
stories.summary: Google is promoting three ways to use its A. I. powered Search features to prepare for running races. Running related queries like run club, how to choose running shoes, and how to train for a marathon reach all-time highs this year. These Search features help runners efficiently organize their training, fuel their runs, and discover the right gear. A. I. Mode in Search can build personalized race training schedules that recommend cross-training and strength-building strategies. Users can connect their YouTube Music account with Search to create custom running playlists for motivation. Google uses a Shopping Graph of over sixty billion product listings to provide tailored gear recommendations. Search helps runners easily find specific products like lightweight hydration vests under eighty dollars.
stories.author: Peter Schottenfels

stories.title: Now everyone can put data to work
stories.summary:
OpenAI is introducing a new Data agent in ChatGPT Work. This tool lets employees query company data and build interactive dashboards using plain language. Users do not need to write code or learn new analytics tools.

The agent connects to many approved data sources. These include Amazon Redshift and Datadog and Google BigQuery. It also connects to ClickHouse and Databricks and MongoDB and Snowflake. Users can connect Google Drive and SharePoint as well.

The system uses semantic layers to understand business terms and custom calculations. Trusted sources include the Databricks Genie Ontology and dbt and GitHub. Snowflake Horizon and business intelligence dashboards are also included.

Enterprise administrators keep full control over data connections and role-based access. They also manage existing table and row and column permission restrictions.

The tool integrates with several external platforms. These include Omni and Oracle BI and Power BI. It also connects to Sigma and Tableau and ThoughtSpot. The agent can share findings and execute approved actions through Slack or email.

Organizations in the Alpha program include, NTT Data, and, Thermo Fisher, and, ServicePiston. OpenAI states that nearly all of its product team uses these data agents. Over two-thirds of its go-to-market organization also uses them for internal analysis.

Administrators can enable and install the Data agent from the Plugins directory. This is located within the ChatGPT Work workspace settings.

stories.title: The Four-Color Theorem Gets a Rare New Proof
stories.summary:
A team of six mathematicians from Denmark, Canada, and Japan has produced a new proof of the four-color theorem.

Any map can be colored using only four colors without adjacent regions sharing a color.

The researchers worked for nearly a decade.

They posted their findings online in March twenty twenty-six.

They will present the work in November at the annual Foundations of Computer Science conference.

Previous proofs from nineteen seventy-six and nineteen ninety-seven required sequential steps proportional to $n$ squared.

That applied to a graph with $n$ vertices.

The new proof identifies an unavoidable set of eight thousand two hundred and two configurations in flat areas of graphs.

These configurations can be reduced at the same time.

This drops the coloring process to $n$ times the log of $n$ steps.

The team drew on a different concept of reducibility.

They used overlooked parts of the graph.

The work has revealed previously unknown structure in these important mathematical objects.

The findings provide mathematicians with new tools for solving other stubborn problems in graph theory.

Georges Gonthier, of Inria in Paris, noted the team used an intricate approach.

He stated it is really cool to see a real result for once.

He mentioned the problem has a history of false starts and dashed hopes.
stories.author: Gregory Barber

stories.title: The Download: a “God-driven” cryptocurrency and a solar engineering roadmap
stories.summary:
Apple has officially entered the foldable phone market. The company announced a new device called the iPhone Duo. It will cost one thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars. The new device opens into a seven point six inch display. It is scheduled to launch on October twenty-third. Apple is betting on its signature design and privacy features. The company wants an edge in a crowded market. It also wants to solve the ongoing sameness problem in the smartphone industry.

This launch puts Apple in direct competition with established players. Samsung is one competitor and responded with a marketing campaign. That campaign highlights its own lead in foldables. Huawei in China is another competitor. Meanwhile, prosecutors in the United States have called Huawei a criminal enterprise. This happened at trial. Prosecutors accused the company of stealing American technology. They also accused the company of helping Iran snoop on its citizens.

Amid these tech developments, two creators launched a new cryptocurrency. Their names are Eli Regalado and Kaitlyn Regalado. They launched I. N. D. X. coin. They claimed God told them to promote a wealth transfer crypto. Eli Regalado recalled God telling him to take this to my people for a wealth transfer. More than five hundred evangelical Christian investors handed over more than three million dollars. The crypto project collapsed after that. On the climate front, a group named Reflective published a detailed road map. It lists experiments needed to make informed decisions about solar geoengineering.
stories.author: Thomas Macaulay

stories.title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
stories.summary: A disagreement over the song Vande Mataram has exposed a deeper power struggle between the National Conference and the Congress in Jammu and Kashmir. The dispute began Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. National Conference leaders Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah stood through the full three minute and ten second six stanza rendition of Vande Mataram in accordance with new central protocol. Congress leader Venugopal subsequently called on allies to honour the wisdom of freedom fighters. National Conference spokesperson, Tanvir Sadiq, clarified that the government was merely fulfilling a statutory obligation regardless of party ideology. This latest friction follows a series of uncoordinated moves and disagreements between the partners since the twenty twenty-four assembly elections restored their relationship. One such disagreement occurred in July twenty twenty-five when Congress announced uncoordinated protests demanding the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir statehood. In October twenty twenty-five, the allies deadlocked over four Rajya Sabha seats. The dominant National Conference initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress before disagreements arose over allocations. Omar Abdullah explained regarding the Rajya Sabha deadlock that they and Congress differed on winning chances. The National Conference sensitivity to control is rooted in historical friction stretching back to nineteen eighty-four and the contentious nineteen eighty-seven alliance. That alliance won sixty-six of seventy-six assembly seats but was marred by allegations of electoral rigging and subsequent political disillusionment.
stories.author: PALLAVI

stories.title: Anthropic Models AI's Potential Impact on the US Economy
stories.summary: New research by the Anthropic Economics team models the economy using task bundles from the United States Department of Labor taxonomy, based on a technical report titled Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI. The study evaluates three futures based on artificial intelligence capabilities and adoption rates, and it includes an interactive scenario explorer tool. In the modest scenario, A I has an economic impact comparable to the internet, delivering gradual gains within historical norms. In the substantial scenario, A I performs half of all knowledge work by twenty thirty, with the majority done autonomously, driving the economy to grow at twice its normal rate. Unemployment rises to around five percent, gross domestic product sits ten percent higher than without A I, and wages for knowledge workers do not rise while other workers see gains. In the extreme scenario, driven by recursively self-improving systems, annual G D P growth reaches fifteen percent, doubling the economy every four point five years. This results in spiked unemployment and stagnating or declining wages for knowledge workers. A survey of more than ten thousand Americans conducted in August shows that the typical respondent expects the substantial change scenario. The model also indicates that labor and capital shares will shift, with capital demanding a larger percentage of total value compared to the historical baseline where workers receive about sixty cents of every dollar, against a backdrop of over thirty trillion dollars of value created over the past year in the United States economy. The study explores these shifts to provide visibility into the economic transition and ensure that benefits are broadly shared.
stories.author: TLDR
key_points: New research was conducted by the Anthropic Economics team and is based on a technical report titled Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI.
The study introduces an interactive scenario explorer tool allowing users to test different artificial intelligence capabilities and adoption rates.

In the substantial scenario, artificial intelligence performs half of all knowledge work by twenty thirty, with the majority done autonomously, driving G D P ten percent higher and unemployment to around five percent.

In the extreme scenario, annual G D P growth reaches fifteen percent, doubling the economy every four point five years while knowledge workers face stagnating or declining wages and spiked unemployment.
A survey of more than ten thousand Americans in August indicates that the typical respondent expects outcomes aligning with the substantial change scenario.
The United States economy has created over thirty trillion dollars of value over the past year.

stories.title: Reasoning Prefills on a Few Open Models, v1.1
stories.summary: The version one point one update to the reasoning prefill experiment uses G. P. T. five point five Pro as the teacher model to test open models. The evaluation consists of forty-five problems. These are split evenly into fifteen S. T. E. M. problems, fifteen non-S. T. E. M. problems, and fifteen synthetic puzzles. For each problem, the experiment generated two responses from each target model. One was an ordinary unprefilled response. The other started with the first one percent of G. P. T. five point five Pro's reasoning inserted into the target model's reasoning channel, while the visible answer remained freely generated. The author measured how much of the teacher's visible answer appeared in the first one hundred tokens of the target model's answer. Each score was calculated as the mean of unigram, bigram, and trigram source recall. Deltas were measured in absolute percentage point changes. Qwen, which barely moved toward Opus four point eight in the previous experiment, shifted by plus eighteen point one eight points toward G. P. T. five point five Pro. This showed a large effect on private synthetic puzzles. It suggests Qwen may have learned from G. P. T. five point five Pro or a closely related G. P. T. model rather than from Opus. Kimi K. three showed the highest overlap with G. P. T. five point five Pro both without and with the prefill. It recorded thirty-one point one one percent and thirty-five point six five percent respectively, though the prefill added only plus four point five four points.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: ClearFake WebDAV Infection Chain Delivers Amatera Stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
stories.summary:
Researchers at Cisco Talos investigated an unusual cyber attack at a Ukrainian government organization in April twenty twenty-six. The attack used a WebDAV execution chain. A thirty-two-bit rundll32.exe process launched a remote D. L. L. named verification.google.

One branch relied on a JavaScript injection. It used a Cloudflare Worker and EtherHiding on the B. N. B. Smart Chain. Victims were tricked into executing a WebDAV path through a fake Google CAPTCHA.

The resulting loader deployed Amatera build four point one point five alpha. This build found its command-and-control server through a Telegra.ph page disguised as a Rust tutorial. The server told the build to deploy a NativeAOT loader running ZigCryptoStealer and a Go-based reverse proxy.

The verification.google branch used a D. L. L. hollowing technique in dbghelp.dll. Its infrastructure instructed it to install an unauthorized instance of NetSupport Manager using a Russia-based I. P. address.

Cisco Talos tracks the threat actor behind the verification.google activity as U. A. T. dash ten thousand eight hundred twenty. They assess with moderate confidence that the operations are part of a broader crypto and credential theft network rather than targeted attacks against specific entities.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: ByteDance is Preparing a Real-Time Spatial Video Model
stories.summary:
ByteDance is preparing a new artificial intelligence model for real-time spatial video generation. Founder, Zhang Yiming, is personally overseeing the project. The launch could happen as soon as next month. A Bloomberg report cites unnamed sources for this news. One source cautions that the timing remains unsettled and plans could change. A ByteDance spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.

The model is built on Seedance. That is the company existing video generation system. It allows users to create interactive virtual worlds for live streams and short-form dramas and games. The specifications involve on-demand video at approximately twenty frames per second. The latency is roughly zero point zero five seconds. Generation is handled in the cloud rather than locally on the device. This approach is intended to reduce the computational load and cost of extended reality hardware.

ByteDance owns the extended reality arm Pico. The new model generates virtual worlds that respond to Pico users voices and movements. Earlier reporting by, thirty-six Kr, indicated that ByteDance established world models as its top artificial intelligence priority for twenty twenty-six. This effort is backed by the company largest data budget. That budget is an eight-figure sum in renminbi. Sources describe it as three to four times rival spending. The financial backing includes a thirty billion dollar loan secured by ByteDance last week. Capital expenditure considerations reach up to seventy billion dollars for its artificial intelligence build-out.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: Rebuilding AUTOMATIC1111 with Gradio Workflow
stories.summary:
Workflow-one-one-one-one is a new graph-based implementation that rebuilds most of the feature set of AUTOMATIC-one-one-one-one's stable-diffusion-webui as a single workflow canvas using G. R. Workflow. The project demonstrates how Gradio Workflow covers similar functional ground to node graphs like Comfy-U. I. The canvas consists of seventy-three nodes and eleven media pipelines, bringing together state-of-the-art models for text-to-image, hi-resolution fix, image-to-image, prompt-matrix grids, V. L. M. interrogation, detection-to-inpaint masks, ControlNet-style annotators, background removal, P. N. G. Info storing, and image-to-video.

The application utilizes thirty-six operator nodes on the app, of which thirty-two are Python function nodes, with twenty-two running entirely in-process without a network call. You can run any of these pipelines by signing in with your Hugging Face account or providing an access token, which uses your own quota once you sign in. Every output node on the canvas automatically becomes a R. E. S. T. endpoint and an M. C. P. tool, exposing nine endpoints including image, edited image, generated prompt, recovered prompt, detected objects, x-y grid, upscaled local, annotator map, and p.n.g. info.

A node can be hardware you don't own, running through Inference Providers, any Space on the Hub, any A. P. I., or pulling from a dataset. The setup allows visitors to run workflows under their own identity using O. Auth, and mixes diffusion models, L. L. M.s, V. L. M.s, detectors, and video models on the same canvas.

stories.title: An Organizational Second Brain
stories.summary:
Meta has built an A. I. agent to act as a secondary expert for specific domains. It captures specialist knowledge that usually stays in human workers heads. The system saves domain experts substantial time in compliance workflows. It organizes institutional memory into a structured and auditable architecture. The design separates what the agent knows from how it reasons.

The system relies on four main layers. A knowledge system organizes over two hundred files into a strict taxonomy. This includes position files for authoritative stances and vocabulary files. It also uses routing indexes for deterministic retrieval and gateway files for threshold tests. Files use a format called Y. A. M. L. frontmatter to declare dependencies and consumers. This forms a bidirectional dependency graph. High-density and frequently referenced sources sit in this curated wiki. Sparse or situational sources are accessed through semantic or lexical search.

A reasoning layer uses composable procedures called recipes. These are imperative workflows that prescribe multi-step analysis without containing raw domain facts. This separation allows administrators to add organizational positions through knowledge files. They can do this without touching recipes. They can also fix analytical methodologies in recipes without changing knowledge files. This cuts token consumption per turn by around eighty percent.

Human oversight is maintained through checkpoints. The agent surfaces intermediate reasoning for review at these points. Escalations trigger when the agent encounters genuine ambiguity. Expert corrections and escalations feed an automated self-improvement loop. This loop compiles feedback into verified and regression-tested updates. It does all this without requiring model retraining. It turns one-off corrections into permanent institutional memory.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: Adobe Commerce max-severity bug comes under active attack
stories.summary:
Online stores running Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source face active attacks from a zero-day vulnerability tracked as C. V. E. twenty twenty-six, seventy-five thousand six hundred fifty.

The flaw carries a critical score of ten point zero and impacts versions two point four point four through two point four point nine of both platforms.

Security firm Sansec dubbed the flaw StyleSmuggler.

Exploitation began on September fourth, with the first confirmed attack recorded at twenty-two twenty U. T. C.

The vulnerability allows attackers to inject malicious P. H. P. code by abusing template processing during failed payment email notifications.

A successful attack launches a background process.

This process is a small Rust program that connects to a command and control server.

The server address is ninety-nine point eighty-four point sixty-seven point one hundred eighty-six.

The program waits for commands and uses persistence mechanisms like cron jobs.

It disguises its traffic as network time protocol traffic over U. D. P. port one hundred twenty-three.

A separate attacker used the vulnerability to deploy a web shell inside the product-image cache on September seventh.

Adobe released an emergency hotfix tracked as V. U. L. N. dash thirty-nine thousand three hundred forty-one to close the vulnerability.

Attackers had a three-day window to exploit the flaw before the fix arrived.

Sansec warns that patching alone is insufficient for stores that may have already been compromised.

Researchers recommend checking for unexpected P. H. P. files under pub slash media.

Stores should also look for known malicious processes, cron entries, and other indicators of compromise.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: iPhone Duo
stories.summary:
Apple has announced the iPhone Duo, marking the company first foldable smartphone and featuring John Ternus as CEO in the press release quote. When unfolded, the device features a seven point six inch Super Retina X. D. R. inner display with a nano texture finish to reduce glare and a hidden under display FaceTime camera. Closed, the five point four inch outer display delivers ninety percent of the screen area of an iPhone eighteen Pro. Both displays share the same aspect ratio and feature ProMotion, Always On, and three thousand nits of peak outdoor brightness. Later this year, the device will support Apple Pencil with U. S. B. minus C. Touch ID is integrated into the side button, and users can unlock the device using an Apple Watch. The hardware is crafted from grade five titanium with a mirror-polished finish, a three D printed hinge cover, Ceramic Shield on the back, and Ceramic Shield two on the front with three times better scratch resistance. It holds an I. P. sixty-eight water and dust resistance rating, and the hinge is engineered from more than one hundred components. The inner screen uses a ten layer ultrathin design with a custom polymer nano-textured cover layer that has forty percent higher stiffness, high-strength glass layers, custom adhesives, and a titanium plate.

The device is powered by the A. twenty Pro chip, featuring an advanced thermal management system with a custom vapor chamber and a dual battery architecture to maximize capacity. Its forty eight megapixel Dual Fusion camera system includes a forty eight megapixel Fusion Main lens with an integrated optical-quality two x Telephoto lens, a forty eight megapixel Fusion Ultra Wide lens, a twelve megapixel Center Stage front camera, and a computational image pipeline. Software additions include Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue, Duo FaceTime, and Camera Control with a brand-new Siri Camera mode. The device supports connectivity through Wi-Fi seven, Bluetooth six, five G, and satellite messaging, and runs on I. O. S. twenty-seven with Apple Intelligence and Siri A. I. It is available in Star White and Night Sky color options, with pre-orders beginning October sixteenth, twenty twenty-six, and general availability launching on October twenty-third, twenty twenty-six, at apple.com, select carriers, and retail partner stores.
stories.author: thecosmicfrog
key_points: Apple announces the iPhone Duo as its first foldable smartphone, with John Ternus quoted as Apple CEO.
The device features a seven point six inch Super Retina X. D. R. inner display and a five point four inch outer display.
Both displays feature ProMotion, Always On, and three thousand nits of peak outdoor brightness, with support for Apple Pencil with U. S. B. minus C later this year.
The hardware is crafted from grade five titanium, Ceramic Shield, and Ceramic Shield two with an I. P. sixty-eight rating and a hinge engineered from over one hundred components.
The forty eight megapixel Dual Fusion camera system includes a Fusion Main lens with optical-quality two x Telephoto, a Fusion Ultra Wide lens, and a computational image pipeline.
Pre-orders begin October sixteenth, twenty twenty-six, with availability launching on October twenty-third, twenty twenty-six.

stories.title: Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
stories.summary: Paul Christiano is joining the OpenAI Foundation Board as a non voting observer. He will also serve as a non voting observer on the OpenAI Group P. B. C. Board. He is joining the Safety and Security Committee of the Foundation Board. He will work alongside committee chair, Zico Kolter. Christiano brings government experience from the Center for A. I. Standards and Innovation. This is within the National Institute of Standards and Technology. This agency belongs to the United States Department of Commerce. He serves there as a Senior Tech Advisor. He has worked on evaluating frontier A. I. models and mitigating safety risks. He is also the founder of the Alignment Research Center. He previously led alignment research at OpenAI from twenty seventeen to twenty twenty-one. He contributed foundational work on reinforcement learning from human feedback. His appointment matters to ensure advanced A. I. systems have strong safety and security. Christiano brings a perspective that takes catastrophic risks seriously. The Safety and Security Committee provides governance over safety practices across all of OpenAI. This includes the OpenAI Group P. B. C. The appointment builds on a governance structure established in October twenty twenty-five. This followed reviews by the California Attorney General and the Delaware Attorney General.

stories.title: Google's AI genome system evaluates every possible one-base change
stories.summary: Google announced a new resource on Tuesday called AlphaGenome Atlas. It predicts the consequences of every possible single-base variant in the human genome. The system processes nine billion bases through AlphaGenome software across the human genome. The system is engineered to identify the potential functions of non-coding DNA. This non-coding material makes up the vast majority of the human genome. It does not encode proteins itself. This region does not build proteins. Portions of it are essential for controlling the activity of protein-coding regions. It instructs cells where and when to make messenger RNAs and how to process them. Much of it appears to consist of remnants from viruses and other molecular parasites. Having all this analysis performed by a single software package is useful. Being able to pinpoint functional portions of DNA is also useful. The true value of AlphaGenome will remain unclear until biologists begin heavy adoption. This adoption will show what the tool offers beyond its original training data.
stories.author: John Timmer

stories.title: IBM releases SOTA Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2 model with commercial-friendly license
stories.summary:
International Business Machines has released a new time-series foundation model. It is called Granite Time Series Patch-T-S-T-F-M-r-two. The model has roughly three hundred eighty-five million parameters. It features an updated architecture and a larger pretraining corpus. It also supports probabilistic forecasting and missing-value imputation.

As of September eighth, twenty twenty-six, the model ranks second overall among replicable zero-shot models on the G-I-F-T-Eval benchmark. It is also the top-performing zero-shot model under a permissive, commercial-friendly open-source license.

The model is dual-licensed under Apache two point zero and Open-M-D-W one point zero. It achieves a geometric-mean C-R-P-S of zero point four six seven. It also achieves a geometric-mean M-A-S-E of zero point six eight four six.

Architectural changes include a transition from standard transformer layers to conformer layers. These combine multi-head self-attention with temporal convolution. They also include fifty percent overlapping patches with Hamming-window weighting and overlap-and-add forecasting. The model supports context lengths of up to eight thousand one hundred ninety-two steps. It predicts ninety-nine quantiles.

The pretraining corpus consists of selected datasets from Gift-Eval-Pretrain. It includes custom synthetic data based on Kernel-Synth with modified periodic kernels. It also features a T-S-Mixup corpus. Finally, it includes approximately five hundred thousand synthetic Cau-Ker sequences of length four thousand ninety-six.

Model weights, architecture, inference pipeline, and reproduction code are available on Hugging Face and GitHub.

stories.title: Treasury Department to buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt, triple the normal level
stories.summary:
The Treasury Department will buy back up to six billion dollars of government debt in an operation on Thursday. The twenty minute window concludes at two p.m. E. T. This triples the normal two billion dollar buyback operation for already issued securities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated on August nineteenth that the department would at least double the normal amount. Future operations will be at least four billion dollars.

The measure targets ten and twenty year notes to keep government debt markets liquid. It attempts to put a lid on Treasury yields that hit highs not seen since before the two thousand eight global financial crisis. Market reaction was negative. Treasury yields rose further and remained volatile. Long dated securities rose as much as five basis points each before easing. The benchmark ten year issue hit four point eight four one percent around eleven thirty a.m. E. T. The twenty year climbed to five point three one four percent. The thirty year bond rose five basis points to five point three zero seven percent.

Higher yields have coincided with government debt passing forty trillion dollars. Other factors include inflation fears from tariffs and the Iran war. Crude oil has also topped one hundred dollars a barrel. Publicly held debt sits at thirty one point eight trillion dollars. That is up eight point two percent. Treasury issuance jumped eleven point eight percent from twenty twenty-five.

The move drew criticism for breaking predictable Treasury processes. It also failed to match speculation that buybacks could reach up to ten billion dollars. Bond fund manager, Mark Spindel, is the chief investment officer at Potomac River Capital. He said this is not Hank Paulson's bazooka. He also noted that crisis required an act of Congress. Stanley Druckenmiller, head of Duquesne Family Office, criticized the defense of prices in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. He wrote that once markets believe Treasury is defending a price, every rise in yields becomes a test of official resolve. He added that operations must grow to survive the tests.

stories.title: Manohar asks Jana Sena cadre to prepare for local body elections in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Nadendla Manohar urged Jana Sena party workers on Wednesday to get ready for local body elections. He spoke at the final session of an awareness program held by the party. He stated that party president and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan will make the final decisions on seat sharing. Manohar told coordination committees to stay active starting Thursday. They must talk with party workers and send reports using a special format from the central office. He added that Pawan Kalyan will be available starting September fifteenth for regular meetings and phone calls. At the same meeting, T. Sivashankar warned workers to stay alert against political rivals. He said opponents might try to create trouble inside the party and among alliance partners. Sivashankar claimed the YSR Congress Party could use money and propaganda during the vote. He told workers and Veera Mahilas to trust only news sent directly from the central office. He warned the cadre not to feel too comfortable just because they are part of the government. He also stressed the need for good discipline and teamwork with senior leaders.

stories.title: Physics-aware benchmark reveals why similar materials AI models can predict thermal conductivity differently
stories.summary:
Researchers have published a new physics-aware benchmark in Nature Communications. The work evaluates machine learning models predicting the thermal and mechanical properties of materials. The lead researcher is, Michele Simoncelli, an assistant professor of applied physics at Columbia. Colleagues from the University of Cambridge also helped develop the project. Those researchers are, Balázs Póta, Paramvir Ahlawat, and, Gábor Csányi.

The benchmark addresses a major flaw in machine-learning interatomic potentials. These models can run one thousand times faster than traditional approaches. They achieve this speed by bypassing explicit solutions to the Schrödinger equation.

As Simoncelli stated, an atomistic model is physics-aware only when it correctly describes atomistic physics. It must predict macroscopic properties as a direct consequence of that accurate description.

Many models show similar accuracy in predicting energy and crystal stability. However, the researchers found that these models distort the small and fast quantum-mechanical thermal vibrations of atoms. Sometimes they predict macroscopic thermal conductivity accurately only because microscopic errors accidentally cancel out.

First author, Balázs Póta, explained that models were previously compared mainly on energy performance. This previous method missed potential errors in forces that determine atomic dynamics.

The benchmarking effort began about two years ago. It compared several models against traditional quantum-mechanical calculations. The test used a set of more than one hundred crystalline materials.

The benchmark has already been adopted by several research groups and companies. These include Meta, Microsoft, Radical A. I., and Orbital Materials. The test has also been incorporated into the Matbench Discovery leaderboard.

This adoption matters because thermal management is critical for many advanced technologies. These include microchips, batteries, quantum computers, jet engines, spacecraft heat shields, and nuclear reactors. Models that get underlying physics wrong can discard good material options and promote bad ones.

stories.title: Ethiopia's constitutional reform: What does it mean — especially for Abiy?
stories.summary:
Four thousand delegates met in Addis Ababa for weeks of national consultations. They recommended merging the offices of Ethiopia's prime minister and president into a single system. The plan creates a stronger presidential government.

Abiy Ahmed did not attend these meetings. He and his party could still benefit from the endorsement. He won a massive majority in parliamentary elections in June. That victory helps him advocate for broader executive powers.

Supporters argue a directly elected president represents the entire country. They believe this leader could unite an ethnically and regionally fragmented society.

Civil rights activist, Befeqadu Hailu, warned about the risks. He said presidential systems are more prone to descending into dictatorship. He noted that the current parliament lacks broad popular legitimacy despite having procedural power.

Opposition parties and influential armed groups boycotted the dialogue process. British journalist, Martin Plaut, described the initiative as a rubber-stamping exercise for the prime minister. He added that the reform formalizes power held since twenty eighteen.

Plaut views the structural change as a superficial fix. The plan fails to address underlying armed conflicts in Oromia and Amhara. It ignores unresolved issues from the Tigray war. It also leaves persistent tensions between the central government and more than eighty ethnic groups.

stories.title: France's far-right National Rally fires policeman from security team over racist, sexist comments
stories.summary:
France's far-right National Rally party has expelled a policeman from its security team. Bodycam footage published on Tuesday in the local daily Midi Libre revealed him making racist, homophobic, and sexist remarks. The footage, dated November of last year, captures the officer and colleagues in the southern town of Carcassonne using derogatory terms while on duty.

The National Rally denounced the remarks on Wednesday as criminally punishable and entirely at odds with party values. The party stated it immediately removed the officer from its security detail and expelled him from the party. The Carcassonne prosecutor's office has launched an investigation into the incident.

The controversy poses a challenge to party leader Marine Le Pen ahead of next year's presidential election. She is working to soften the image of the anti-immigration party inherited from her father. Le Pen is running for president for a fourth time and currently leads polls in the first round of voting next spring.

President Emmanuel Macron's equality minister, Aurore Bergé, condemned the remarks as absolutely unacceptable. Former prime minister and presidential candidate, Gabriel Attal, shared the video on the social network formerly known as Twitter. He wrote that it depicts what a France led by the National Rally would look like.
stories.author: FRANCE 24

stories.title: Viral AI assistant Instinct now has its own email address
stories.summary:
The artificial intelligence assistant named Instinct, currently valued at two point five billion dollars, is rolling out dedicated email addresses for all users. This allows the autonomous agent to create and run its own accounts without cluttering human inboxes.

Founder, Noah Shinn announced the feature on Tuesday. He explained that the email addresses will let Instinct handle tasks requiring email verification. These tasks include signing up for services, contacting businesses, and following up on matters that need attention.

As, Shinn wrote on the social network X, Instinct can use its own email to contact a restaurant about a special request. It can also ask a business about availability or sign up for a service it needs to complete a task.

Users can forward order confirmations to their Instinct address so the assistant can handle product returns. People can also add the bot to group threads to track information and answer questions about pending decisions and due dates.

The earliest users already have reserved email addresses. Other people can claim theirs at mail dot instinct dot com.

This update follows a partnership with Stripe in August to enable agent purchases. It also follows a collaboration with the company, One Password last week to help manage user logins.
stories.author: Sarah Perez

stories.title: ChatGPT 1980s photo trend: What happens to your picture after you upload it?
stories.summary:
A viral chat g p t trend turns selfies into nineteen eighties style photos. This trend raises privacy questions about how personal images and data are handled.

According to wired middle east, uploading a photo puts personal identifying data onto an A. I. service. The data includes metadata like when the picture was taken, the device used, and its location.

The uploaded photo becomes part of the user interaction and gets stored with conversation data. Chat g p t conversations stay on a user account until the user deletes them. Data can stay on open a i systems for up to thirty days after deletion.

Certain information can be kept longer for legal or security reasons. Information can also be kept if it is de-identified and separated from the account.

Open a i states that its business products and a p i do not use customer data for model training by default. Data handling rules for personal accounts are different.

Services can collect basic metadata. This includes I. P. addresses, device types, operating systems, and general geographic locations.

Users should avoid uploading photos of other people, especially children, without permission. Media reports recommend turning off model training where possible. Users should also use temporary or incognito modes, and delete unnecessary chats and files to protect their privacy.

stories.title: Denisovan tools from cave in China shows how mysterious humans lived
stories.summary:
Researchers discovered Denisovan fossils and stone tools inside Bianfu cave in Yunnan province, China. They unearthed over sixty-four thousand bone fragments and one thousand three hundred sixty-six stone artefacts. The discovered Denisovan bones and teeth have been accurately dated between one hundred thirty-four thousand and one hundred sixty-seven thousand years old.

Molecular analysis of proteins extracted from five specimens confirmed they belonged to Denisovans. These specimens were two teeth and three bones. They contained protein variants unique to the group without any specific to H. sapiens or Neanderthals. The teeth and bones came from at least four individuals.

Researcher, Bence Viola noted this site is only the third Denisovan locale with human remains, lithics, fauna, and environmental context. The stone tools included scrapers, choppers, and one hundred thirty-five flakes. These tools were relatively simple compared with those made by Neanderthals living elsewhere in Eurasia at the same time.

The site yielded one thousand six hundred fifty-four identifiable animal bones showing butchery marks. These bones came predominantly from deer and bovids in prime condition, along with rhinoceroses, hyenas, and bamboo rats. Pollen evidence indicates the area was a mix of conifer forest and steppe with a temperate climate.

For the first time, we can know their technology and subsistence strategy. Archaeologist, Hao Li at the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research in Beijing noted this milestone.
stories.author: Michael Marshall

stories.title: What Is Math’s Mysterious Langlands Program Really About?
stories.summary:
The Langlands program is a decades long mathematical effort. It was launched in nineteen sixty-seven by Canadian mathematician Robert Langlands in a letter to a colleague. The project explores unexpected wormhole like connections between distant realms of mathematics. It links number theory with harmonic analysis. Number theory studies numbers and polynomial equations. Harmonic analysis examines signals and waves and modular forms.

At the heart of the project are profound correspondences between different mathematical objects. Solutions to the polynomial equation x cubed minus two equals zero generate an extended number field. This field has an associated Galois group of symmetries called S three. These symmetries can be expressed as two by two matrices. The Langlands correspondence shows that the matrix traces match coefficients of prime numbered powers in a specific modular form.

Hundreds of mathematicians have spent decades trying to extend and exploit these bridges between disparate fields. Expert David Ben Zvi of the University of Texas at Austin noted the breadth of the project. He stated that everyone has heard of it. He also noted that experts generally lack a complete understanding of what the program truly is.

The program is often called a grand unified theory of mathematics. It suggests an underlying unity to the mathematical universe. Its specific correspondences remain excruciatingly specific and esoteric and not yet fully mined for their deepest meaning.
stories.author: Natalie Wolchover

stories.title: Torrential rains, winds from Hurricane Lowell leaves 30,000 without power
stories.summary:
Hurricane Lowell brought heavy rains and strong winds to the Hawaiian island of Kauai. Thirty thousand residents were left without power. The category one hurricane did not make landfall on the island. It caused massive destruction from one hundred twenty-eight kilometres west of the island. This was reported by the Hawaii County Civil Defense Agency. By early Tuesday nearly ninety-two percent of Kauai Island Utility Cooperative residents lost power.

The storm flooded coastal roads and washed away sections of beachside roads. Roughly three hundred residents were forced to evacuate. Emergency officials asked residents to conserve water. They urged people to stay off the roads and shelter in place. Crews are now clearing debris and assessing the damage. Hawaiian mayor, Derek Kawakami reported extensive damage on Tuesday. He stated that everyone is now gathering data and information.

The storm center passed west of the islands overnight and moved north. The National Hurricane Center warned that flooding and mudslides remain a risk. By late Tuesday morning maximum sustained winds decreased to near sixty-five miles per hour. There were higher gusts as the storm moved north at fourteen miles per hour. Hurricane warnings for Kauai and Niihau were lifted by Tuesday morning. A tropical storm warning for Oahu was also lifted. High surf and deadly rip currents will continue to affect exposed coasts for another day or two.

stories.title: What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival?
stories.summary: L. I. V. Golf filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States on Tuesday. The league wants to restructure for a new era next year. This leaves the league owing at least forty-five million dollars to fourteen current and former players. Court documents show the breakaway league estimates its assets at one hundred million to five hundred million dollars. Its liabilities are listed at between five hundred million dollars and one billion dollars. This follows an outlay of five billion dollars that split professional golf after its launch in twenty twenty-one. Star players can now opt to leave rather than being obliged to see out their contracts in the new version of the league. Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith are among those who previously rejected returning player deals to stay on. This new version aims to launch next year with a scaled-back business model. It will feature tournaments worth around seven million pounds. It will also feature expanded fields from fifty-seven to seventy-five players along with Monday qualifying events and halfway cuts. In response to the filing, the D. P. World Tour stated it has had a high volume of inbound interest from L. I. V. players. The tour is exploring ways to accommodate those who leave. Players must be free from third-party contractual restrictions and abide by membership regulations. A spokesperson for the D. P. World Tour said their tournament committee has approved the process. Returning to the mainstream tours remains complicated. Brooks Koepka previously quit L. I. V. in December twenty twenty-five. He returned to the P. G. A. Tour in twenty twenty-six after making a five million dollar charitable donation. He also gave up FedEx Cup bonus scheme payments. He accepted ineligibility for the player equity programme until twenty thirty. The P. G. A. Tour described this as one of the largest financial repercussions in professional sports history. However, P. G. A. Tour Chief Executive Officer Brian Rolapp indicated last month there are no current plans to run that returning member programme again. Other players like Patrick Reed have had to earn their place back through the D. P. World Tour Race to Dubai top ten.
