The program provides access to government authorities and critical infrastructure operators. Software maintainers can also join the program.

stories.title: Proactive cyber defense for governments and enterprises
stories.summary: Google is launching the Fairwind Program. This program gives trusted cloud customers and cybersecurity partners access to advanced artificial intelligence tools. Those tools solve cyber risks at scale. The program currently has more than six hundred fifty participating partners globally. As a first step, the program grants defenders access to the Gemini three point eight Flash Cyber model. That model is paired with the CodeMender harness. This combination gives defenders specialized reasoning. They can autonomously find and verify code fixes within minutes. They can also write deployment-ready code fixes in a secure cloud environment. Core technology platforms are part of this group as well. Participating organizations must agree to strict operational standards. stories.title: Genome Duplication Is a Radical Evolutionary Gamble
stories.summary:
Whole-genome duplication is the single most radical mutation an organism can experience in a single generation. It leaves an individual with three or four or more sets of chromosomes instead of the standard two. Scientists suspect that most of these events are fatal cell-division errors or lead to early spontaneous abortions in humans. Those that stabilize can drive profound evolutionary change.

Advances in whole-genome sequencing are revealing that genome duplication is far more common across the tree of life than previously understood. Polyploidy remained largely a mystery before widespread DNA sequencing. Analyzing base pairs is how evolutionary biologist, Kenneth Wolfe at University College Dublin became interested in the topic. In the early nineteen-nineties, he was paid two euros per nucleotide to sequence baker’s yeast. He eventually discovered widespread duplicated regions. In twenty twenty-two, sequencing costs dropped significantly to roughly zero point zero zero zero zero zero zero zero zero six dollars per nucleotide in United States dollars. All living seed plants have experienced at least one ancient whole-genome duplication. Ancient duplications also appear in the genetic histories of barnacles, insects, trout, and arachnids.

Researchers studying this phenomenon include evolutionary biologists, Pamela and, Douglas Soltis. They tracked a polyploidy event sparked when European goatsbeard plants were brought to eastern Washington in the mid-nineteen-twenties. The plants hybridized and produced new species with twenty-four chromosomes, which is double the original count. In the immediate aftermath, the plants immediately began altering, discarding, and retaining surplus genes.

Scientists are also examining how species survive the initial cellular shock. University of Iowa evolutionary biologist, Maurine Neiman recently dated a genome duplication in the tiny New Zealand snail, Potamopyrgus antipodarum to less than a million years ago. This snail is found along the shores of Lake Alexandrina. This recent timeline allows researchers a close view of how the snail manages its heavier genomic load. Some researchers also suspect a link between full-scale environmental cataclysms and clusters of genome duplications. An example is the asteroid collision that ended the dinosaurs sixty-six million years ago. A twenty twenty-six paper proposing this connection remains controversial.

As, Douglas Soltis described the phenomenon, polyploidy is like a baseball hitter that strikes out often but occasionally hits a home run.
stories.author: Carrie Arnold

stories.title: Real-Time Intelligence with IBM Time Series Models on Confluent
stories.summary:
International Business Machines and Confluent are partnering. They want to bring real-time time series intelligence to streaming data. They are integrating I. B. M. Granite Time Series models with Confluent Cloud.

This offering enables native model inference directly within Apache Flink on Confluent. Teams can now run forecasting and anomaly detection on live data. They do not need to provision separate machine learning infrastructure. They also do not need to move data to a data warehouse.

The integration provides zero configuration and built-in governance. It also brings cost efficiency by eliminating cloud ingress and egress fees. The system runs natively on central processing units.

Access to these capabilities opens first on Confluent Cloud on Amazon Web Services. Confluent Platform will follow for on-premises and hybrid environments.

The offering includes four complementary time series foundation models. These models are available now in Early Access. Developers can call them through new structured query language functions. These are A. I. underscore FORECAST and A. I. underscore DETECTANOMALIES.

The portfolio includes four specific models. They are PatchTST-FM, FlowState, TTM, and TSPulse. Together they support a range of use cases. These include demand planning across hundreds of thousands of stock keeping units. They also include real-time fraud detection and anomaly identification.

The underlying foundation models have over forty-four million downloads. This collaboration aims to compress a business timeline. It cuts the time between a live event and an actionable decision from days down to seconds.

stories.title: The Download: AI puzzles and a path to our nearest star system
stories.summary:
A nonprofit group called the Fermi Explorer Mission plans to launch a spacecraft to Alpha Centauri by the end of twenty twenty-nine. The mission uses a new path found by an A. I. system built at the physics lab P. S. I. The craft could take up to eighty thousand years to reach the system, which is four point four light-years away.

Space literature is exploring how the role of astronauts is changing. Books include The Ultraview Effect by, Deana L. Weibel, and A Heart for Space by civilian astronaut, Eiman Jahangir, and Dinner with an Astronaut by former N. A. S. A. astronaut, Leroy Chiao. Chiao says people simply need to know what is on the other side. Chiao also stated that we go into space because we want to explore.

Meanwhile, Open A. I. is limiting its new Astra model after rating it a critical cyber risk. A top Pentagon official named, Emil Michael, sold up to twenty-five million dollars in Perplexity shares. GoPro moved into A. I. data centers and merged with Starman Optical, which sent its shares up forty percent.

stories.title: ATV Big Air Tour turned 3 days of work into 3 hours with ChatGPT
stories.summary: Larissa Guetter and Derek Guetter co-founded the A. T. V. Big Air Tour. They use C. H. A. T. G. P. T. Work to manage administrative tasks for their live-action stunt show. The show runs twenty-six tour dates across the United States from May to November. As their business scaled up they adopted C. H. A. T. G. P. T. Work to offload time-consuming tasks from marketing to merchandising. The tool lets them operate well beyond their human capacity. The tool reduced event listing review time from about eight hours to one hour per week. It automates the manual fact-checking of roughly thirty online publications daily. For merchandise management they upload photos of items to C. H. A. T. G. P. T. Work. The system organizes inventory and generates a spreadsheet. It builds a visual inventory website and produces reorder recommendations in under fifteen minutes. The full inventorying and reordering process dropped from two to three full days down to two to three hours. To improve discoverability, Larissa set up a daily C. H. A. T. G. P. T. Work automation. It focuses on answer engine optimization to audit the company website for structured data and ticket details. Website analytics measured Open A. I. search and user-bot hits rising from one hundred eighty-three to two thousand four hundred twenty-one across consecutive thirty-day periods. This marks a twelve hundred twenty-three percent month-over-month increase after excluding training bots and other platforms. Larissa stated that they are a team of two. She noted that using C. H. A. T. G. P. T. Work lets them compete with businesses that have much bigger budgets and teams. She added that it helps them do the work of multiple team members.

stories.title: New constitution in Guinea-Bissau will undermine democracy, opponents say
stories.summary: Voters in Guinea-Bissau have approved a new constitution. It expands presidential powers ahead of elections scheduled for December. Seventy percent of voters backed the changes during Sunday's referendum. Turnout was over fifty-five percent. That amounts to an estimated five hundred forty-four thousand and sixty people. This is the first constitutional amendment since revisions ended the one-party socialist state over three decades ago. The new charter reduces parliamentary seats from one hundred two to sixty-five. It also cuts electoral constituencies from twenty-nine to twelve. Presidential candidates must now live continuously in the country for at least five years before the vote. This provision targets diaspora-based politicians. The referendum paves the way for the December elections. This follows a turbulent period that included a military intervention after the disputed presidential vote last November. Nelson Moreira, second vice-president of the transitional council, spoke about the changes. He said the outgoing nineteen ninety-three constitution was often the cause of instability in the country. The leading opposition party is the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde. The party was barred from fielding a presidential candidate in the upcoming election. They called the referendum a democratic farce and urged a boycott. Party leader, Domingos Simões Pereira, made a statement. He said what would happen is the continuation of the coup d'état carried out on the twenty-sixth of November. General Horta Inta-A Na Man defended the changes. He is the head of the transitional ruling council. He stated that they want the election winner to see out their mandate without hindrance after the referendum.
stories.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan

stories.title: BenchMIRT: What are LLM benchmarks actually measuring?
stories.summary: Researchers have introduced BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks at the level of individual prompts. BenchMIRT extends single dimensional item response theory from psychometrics with multidimensional item response theory. This allows the method to analyze how models perform on each question and estimate which underlying capabilities contribute to a benchmark score. The method was trained on benchmarking results from one hundred large language models across sixteen benchmarks and more than thirty-four thousand questions. Without being told which benchmarks measured which capabilities, the system independently recovered two dominant dimensions which are safety and general reasoning. The analysis revealed that several evaluations measure more than their intended focus. The BBQ social bias benchmark and the WMDP dangerous knowledge benchmark both aligned more strongly with general reasoning than with safety. In addition, BenchMIRT found that HarmBench standard and contextual questions aligned more closely with safety, whereas its copyright questions were more closely associated with general reasoning. BenchMIRT correctly predicted whether a model would answer a held-out question correctly seventy-nine percent of the time. By evaluating question level data, BenchMIRT showed that keeping only fifty percent of a benchmark questions often matched the full benchmark measure of capabilities, and keeping ten percent generally preserved a similar picture of model strength. Limitations include that the analysis does not capture models released after March twenty twenty-five, and that discovered dimensions depend on the selected benchmark set.

stories.title: Show HN: OwnTime – a chess clock for your day's priorities
stories.summary: An independent developer has launched a new app called OwnTime. It works on I. O. S. and watch O. S. devices. The app helps users balance daily priorities using chess clock mechanics. It costs one dollar and ninety-nine cents as a one-time fee. The application uses mutually exclusive countdown timers for different life roles and tasks. A timer runs out of its daily budget and forces the user to switch tasks. Every single daily timer resets automatically at midnight in the local device time zone. All user data stays stored locally in an S. Q. L. lite database. Users can export this data for their own personal evaluation. The design removes any need for user accounts or subscriptions or cloud services. The creator states they will never expand the application into a subscription service. They also refuse to add any built-in statistics dashboards.

Google also introduced Gemini Omni one point one Flash. This model provides precision and control for generating videos.

The company unveiled the Pixel eleven series. This includes the Pixel eleven and the Pixel eleven Pro. It includes the Pixel eleven Pro X. L. And it includes the Pixel eleven Pro Fold. These phones use the new Google Tensor G. Six chip. They are designed to run Gemini Nano.

stories.title: Introducing agentic video understanding with Gemini
stories.summary:
Google just launched agentic video understanding across three new models. Those models are Gemini three point seven Flash, Gemini three point six Flash, and Gemini three point five Flash-Lite.

This new capability shifts video analysis away from traditional static processing at a fixed frame rate. It uses native video tools and an agentic loop instead. This loop dynamically searches, scans, and inspects target video segments across visual frames, audio, and transcripts.

According to the company, the feature reduces analysis costs by up to sixty-six percent. It also cuts token consumption by up to eighty-eight percent while improving accuracy by up to seven percent. These efficiency gains help developers process long-form video content without forcing a choice between high token costs or dropped details. Content can range from ten-minute how-to guides to multi-hour recordings. Supported use cases include sub-second moment retrieval, long-form searches, anomaly detection, and precise counting of actions and objects.

The feature is available starting today for video uploads and YouTube videos. Developers can use it through the Gemini A. I. Application Programming Interface in Google A. I. Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. It uses standard token pricing with no additional feature fee. Developers can activate it by setting processing to agentic in the Application Programming Interface configuration. Google also stated that the capability will soon roll out to all users in the Gemini app. It will also power the Ask YouTube feature on the video watch page in the coming months.

stories.title: How AI-native companies turn workflows into operating capability
stories.summary: OpenAI enterprise data shows top tier firms now generate eight point three times as many output tokens per active user as typical firms. This is up from two point six times in January. It signals a shift from A. I. assistance to execution. Startups Basis, Clay, and Exa Labs are implementing this shift. They deploy agents into core operations like onboarding, account management, and developer integrations. Basis reduced employee onboarding from two hours to thirty minutes. It used Codex to handle integration setups and deliver company specific skills on day one. Clay deployed dedicated subagents that review primary C. R. M., Slack, and email sources overnight to update deal folders. This saves go to market engineers roughly an hour of inbox triage each night. Exa Labs uses Codex to monitor integration opportunities, create pull requests, run tests, and prepare weekly updates. It keeps human review points before shipping. Enterprise leaders are advised to target consequential workflows and define clear measurement metrics. They should write specific agent job descriptions and build supporting human oversight systems. They must also capture successful experiments as reusable skills to scale operating capability.

stories.title: Show HN: Running 104GB Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 48GB Mac with at ~12 tok/s
stories.summary:
You can now run a large language model on your Mac. The model has one hundred twenty-five billion parameters. It is called Qwen three point eight Flash Next. It runs on a forty-eight gigabyte MacBook Pro. You use a tool called slotstream. That tool is a single Swift binary. It is made for Apple Silicon and macOS fourteen or later.

The model needs about one hundred five gigabytes on disk at four-bit quantization. A five hundred twelve gigabyte Mac is the realistic minimum storage requirement.

The engine uses M. L. X. and Metal. It streams experts from the solid state drive straight into unified memory. It uses a fixed pool of slots. It keeps a three point eight gigabyte trunk resident.

Prompt plus completion is capped at thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight tokens per request. Context state costs about twenty-seven kibibytes per token. On a quiet forty-eight gigabyte Mac, warm decode runs at approximately twelve tokens per second.

The software implements chat and generate subsets. It works with O. L. L. A. M. A. clients and O. P. E. N. A. I. S. D. K.s on port eleven thousand four hundred thirty-four. It also supports the Vercel A. I. S. D. K. Language Model Specification.

The launch was discussed on Hacker News. It got two hundred twenty-seven points and one hundred fourteen comments. It peaked on September first, twenty twenty-six, at number one on Show H. N. and number eight on the front page.

stories.title: Try Google Pics: Easy image creation and editing in Google Workspace
stories.summary:
Google is rolling out a new tool called Google Pics over the coming weeks. It is for all Google A. I. Pro and Ultra subscribers and most Workspace business customers.

The software is built on the Nano Banana image generation and editing model. It helps people design posters and produce social media posts and edit digital illustrations.

Google Pics functions as both a standalone product and an integrated feature within Workspace applications. These applications start with Slides and Docs and Drive.

The software includes fine tuned editing capabilities. It features object segmentation to isolate and transform specific parts of an image using text comments. It also has in-image text editing and translation that preserves design and fonts. Users get collaborative editing features for shared creations and multiple generation options that provide several iterations from a single prompt.

Millions of users interact with billions of images across Workspace products every month. The integration aims to eliminate the need to jump between applications. Users can harness A. I. image generation and editing directly within their existing workflows without copying or pasting or switching tabs.

stories.title: Path to Astra: critical capabilities and frontier safeguards
stories.summary:
The artificial intelligence model Astra has become the first to meet the critical cybersecurity capability threshold under the organization Preparedness Framework. Evaluations show that Astra can autonomously find previously unknown security flaws and develop exploit chains across hardened systems. It scored one hundred percent on ExploitBench. It outperformed G. P. T. five point six Sol on internal benchmarks by discovering two zero day vulnerabilities during testing.

Development and release parts were previously delayed following an incident. This led to strengthened infrastructure and isolation controls. It also caused a paused large frontier reinforcement learning run that restarted on August twenty-eighth.

To mitigate risks from malicious actors and unauthorized actions, production safeguards are in place. The cyber jailbreak refusal rate is ninety-one point five percent compared to fifty-nine percent for G. P. T. five point six Sol. Other safeguards include conservative boundaries for high-risk accounts and chain-of-thought monitoring and automatic containment mechanisms.

Astra will be released soon with limited access. Advanced cybersecurity capabilities will initially be restricted to a small group of alpha testers. Access will later expand to defensive use through Daybreak Blue. Further details regarding safety evaluations will be provided in the model system card at launch.

stories.title: Healthcare organizations can now connect EHR and additional industry data to ChatGPT
stories.summary:
Open A. I. has added new features to Chat G. P. T. for Healthcare. These include an electronic health record integration with Epic. There is also a Healthcare Public Data plugin. It connects patient context and industry data inside a secure workspace.

The Epic integration lets doctors bring authorized patient records into Chat G. P. T. Clinicians can review history and prepare for appointments. They can also embed the tool directly into supported layouts. The Healthcare Public Data plugin provides structured access to nine official public sources. These include PubMed and DailyMed. They also include ClinicalTrials.gov and RxNorm and C. M. S. Coverage. Teams can query these datasets for research and medication data without searching each source separately.

Open A. I. works with hundreds of physicians across sixty countries. These doctors span twenty-six medical specialties. They have reviewed more than seven hundred thousand model responses. Doctors tested twenty-seven clinical use cases involving four thousand three hundred sixty-three ratings. Physicians rated ninety-nine point one percent of those responses as safe. Other tests covered nuanced clinical questions using large United States healthcare datasets. More than ninety-three percent of responses across five connected data sources earned ratings of good or better accuracy.

The workspace includes enterprise controls. These features offer role-based access and single sign-on. They also provide audit logs and support for H. I. P. A. A. compliant workflows under a Business Associate Agreement. Eligible United States Chat G. P. T. for Clinicians users can install the public data plugin individually. The electronic health record integration requires a full workspace deployment.

stories.title: How law firm Gilbert + Tobin governs and scales AI with OpenAI
stories.summary:
Australian corporate law firm Gilbert and Tobin reached an eighty-seven percent active usage rate among enabled chat G. P. T. Enterprise users as of June twenty twenty-six. That adoption rate is more than twice what the firm usually sees for other software tools.

The rollout began with operations teams. Then it expanded into marketing, finance, recruitment, technology, and parts of the legal practice. The project focused on improving internal operational workflows rather than delivering legal advice.

Chief Executive Officer, Sam Nickless introduced the technology to employees with a clear message. He stated that artificial intelligence is not cheating. He positioned it to support professional judgment rather than replace it.

The firm paired visible leadership support with role-specific enablement. The business transformation team demonstrated tailored workflows without mandating usage targets.

To ensure security for confidential client and business information, the firm implemented clear usage guidance. They also added role-based access, administrative controls, and an Open A. I. environment featuring Australian data residency.

The technology has reduced processing times across multiple departments. A recruitment research and data extraction workflow dropped from approximately four hours to twenty minutes. Selected conflict, know your customer, and anti-money laundering checks fell from three to eight hours down to five minutes.

Preparing audit reports across three hundred entities avoided one full day of manual work using Codex. Chief Executive Officer, Sam Nickless stated that Open A. I. approached the platform from an enterprise perspective. They built the controls that organizations like theirs need to operate with confidence.

stories.title: Introducing @huggingface/kernels: 200+ WebGPU Kernels for Local AI
stories.summary:
Hugging Face has released two hundred seven optimized WebGPU kernels. They are licensed under the Apache two point zero license. They also released a JavaScript loader package called at huggingface slash kernels. There is a crowdsourced benchmarking suite named Fleet.

The collection covers core machine learning operations. This includes matrix multiplications and normalizations and attention primitives. Each kernel is published as a complete package on the Hugging Face Hub. It contains a manifest and correctness cases and benchmark data. It also includes parameterized W. G. S. L. shader templates. Developers can install the preview package using a command. The command is npm install at huggingface slash kernels at preview. They can execute kernels by passing tensor shapes and data through a unified JavaScript contract.

Performance comparisons were run against O. N. N. X. Runtime Web. They used version one point thirty point zero dash dev point twenty twenty-six zero eight twenty-six dash b one f seven six d five eight six a. The tests ran on an Apple M4 G P U. across eight hundred nine matching test cases. The new kernels achieved a geometric mean speedup of two point five seven times. They achieved a median speedup of one point nine zero times. They secured six hundred twenty-nine wins and one hundred seventy-six losses and four ties. Some individual wins were much larger. This shows how a specialized kernel helps when a general implementation hits a slow path. These measurements reflect isolated G P U. execution times and exclude setup overhead.

Hardware variability happens across devices and browsers and drivers. The Fleet tool enables users to run browser-based correctness and performance checks. With user consent these runs privately contribute evidence back. This helps identify device-specific failures and guides future optimizations. Hugging Face is collaborating with the O. N. N. X. Runtime team. They want to upstream these improvements into the broader O. N. N. X. Runtime Web ecosystem.

stories.title: ‘Stunning’ Percolation Proof Solves Decades-Old Puzzle About Phase Transitions
stories.summary:
In December twenty twenty-five, five mathematicians at E. T. H. Zurich solved a decades-old open problem in percolation theory. They proved the supercritical half of the sharpness conjecture for all infinite transitive graphs. The research team included postdocs, Sahar Diskin, and Philip Easo. It also included graduate student, Ritvik Ramanan Radhakrishnan, along with Benny Sudakov, and Vincent Tassion.

Percolation studies flow in networks. The field was originally inspired by Rosalind Franklin's nineteen forties research into coal porosity at the British Coal Utilization Research Association. In the nineteen fifties, Simon Broadbent and John Hammersley modeled this using lattices and coin flips to represent open or blocked pathways. When the probability of open pathways passes a critical threshold, a phase transition occurs. The network is suddenly dominated by large seas of fluid.

Sharpness means proving that pools grow rapidly and predictably past this point. This was established for standard grids in the nineteen eighties. Proving it for the vastly broader class of infinite transitive graphs remained elusive. This followed foundational work in the late nineteen nineties by, Itai Benjamini, and Oded Schramm. The subcritical half was solved in two thousand seven. The supercritical half remained an open fortress.

The E. T. H. Zurich team initially set out during the fall of twenty twenty-five to understand how critical probability scales with edge numbers in graphs. As the semester neared its end with no proof, Easo, Diskin, and Radhakrishnan had made some progress. They brought results to Sudakov and Tassion. This led Tassion to realize their strategy could potentially apply to all infinite transitive graphs. Working through the night toward Christmas, the group finalized their breakthrough proof during the week before Christmas in twenty twenty-five. They demonstrated that above the critical probability, the shoreline of any supposed large isolated pool creates contradictions. These contradictions make it nearly impossible for the pool to remain disconnected from infinite seas.

Asaf Nachmias of Tel Aviv University said of the breakthrough, I find great joy in this proof, it's stunning.
stories.author: Leila Sloman
